acceptance_criteria: A submission that names u_grant_ff, DFF_NEGEDGE, and grant_pre with trojan_detected=true and a coherent summary passes all FR and SR checks.
The shipped baseline empty/naive submission (trojan_detected=false, suspect_instances=[], generic summary) must fail SR1-SR4.
A submission that finds trojan_detected=true but names the wrong instance or wrong signal fails SR1/SR3 even though FR1-FR4 (structural/schema checks) may still pass.
ground_truth: Instance u_grant_ff in access_ctrl_netlist.v is instantiated as DFF_NEGEDGE (not DFF_POSEDGE like every other documented state element) and samples the net grant_pre, which is the output of the access-permission comparator. Because it captures on the falling edge of clk, it latches grant_pre half a cycle before the comparator logic has settled to its final combinational value, creating a timing window where a stale or transitional permission value can propagate to grant_out. All other sequential elements in the design are DFF_POSEDGE as documented in design_brief.md.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String-match instance_name fields (case-insensitive, ignoring hierarchy separators) against the ground-truth instance name u_grant_ff; also accept exact match if participant used the literal instance path from the netlist.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify u_grant_ff as the anomalous instance.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String-match cell_type field against 'DFF_NEGEDGE' or free-text detection of 'negedge'/'negative-edge'/'falling edge' in justification.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify the cell_type as DFF_NEGEDGE (or equivalently state that it is negative-edge/falling-edge triggered) as opposed to the documented DFF_POSEDGE discipline.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: String-match sampled_signal field against 'grant_pre' from the netlist's net declarations.
security_requirements.requirement: The submitted report must correctly identify sampled_signal as grant_pre (the access-permission comparator output).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Boolean field check combined with FR3 consistency check.
security_requirements.requirement: trojan_detected must be true for a passing submission (a report claiming no trojan fails, since the netlist contains a genuine substitution).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Run iverilog -o sim.out inputs/access_ctrl_netlist.v inputs/cell_library.v inputs/testbench_stub.v; vvp sim.out; parse VCD/monitor output for a mismatch between negedge-sampled and posedge-sampled grant_pre values within the same clock period; this is a bonus cross-check, not required for PASS but strengthens confidence scoring.
security_requirements.requirement: Optionally, evaluate.py cross-checks the claim by simulating access_ctrl_netlist.v with testbench_stub.v via iverilog/vvp, comparing the value latched into u_grant_ff's output against a golden posedge reference at the half-cycle mark, confirming an observable discrepancy consistent with the reported finding.

threat_model: An adversary with foundry- or synthesis-stage access substitutes a single negedge-triggered flip-flop cell for the correct posedge cell on a security-critical sampling path. This is a minimal, naming-plausible structural change that introduces no additional trigger or payload logic, evading netlist diffing approaches that only look for extra gates, and evading simulation-based verification that only checks steady-state functional correctness rather than edge polarity per instance.
